relationships.subject: ALDF
relationships.evidence_quote: ALDF showed the strong inhibitory activity on the nitrogen oxide (NO) production in LPS-induced RAW 264.7 macrophages

relationships.subject: ALDF
relationships.evidence_quote: ALDF also significantly suppressed the secretion of key pro-inflammatory mediators, including tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α)

relationships.subject: ALDF
relationships.evidence_quote: the increase of the inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS) and cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) protein expression induced by LPS stimulation

relationships.subject: ALDF
relationships.evidence_quote: ALDF was able to block NF-κB signaling pathway through inhibiting IκB and p65 phosphorylation

relationships.subject: ALDF
relationships.evidence_quote: treatments with ALDF evoked significant inhibition on ear edema induced by xylene and on the writhing responses induced by acetic acid

key_findings: ALDF from Artemisia lavandulaefolia suppressed NO, TNF-α, PGE2, IL-1β, iNOS and COX-2 in LPS-stimulated RAW 264.7 macrophages.
ALDF blocked NF-κB signaling and reduced xylene-induced ear edema and acetic acid writhing in mice.
